events.title: Battle of Lepanto
events.description: A fleet of the Catholic Holy League, organized by Pope Pius V and led by Don John of Austria, decisively defeated the Ottoman navy in the Gulf of Patras off western Greece. It was one of the largest naval battles in history, fought mainly between galleys.
events.significance: The victory halted Ottoman naval dominance in the Mediterranean and became a symbol of European Christian unity, though the Ottomans rebuilt their fleet quickly.

events.title: Death of Edgar Allan Poe
events.description: American writer, poet, and critic Edgar Allan Poe died in Baltimore, Maryland, at age 40, after being found delirious on the streets days earlier. The cause of his death remains a mystery.
events.significance: Poe pioneered the modern detective story and shaped the Gothic and horror genres, influencing literature worldwide.

events.title: Founding of the German Democratic Republic
events.description: The German Democratic Republic (East Germany) was established in the Soviet occupation zone, five months after the creation of West Germany. Wilhelm Pieck became its first president.
events.significance: The founding formalized the division of Germany during the Cold War, which lasted until reunification on October 3, 1990.

events.title: US-led invasion of Afghanistan begins
events.description: The United States and the United Kingdom began Operation Enduring Freedom with airstrikes against Taliban and al-Qaeda targets in Afghanistan, in response to the September 11 attacks.
events.significance: It marked the start of the longest war in US history, lasting nearly 20 years and reshaping global security policy and the region's politics.

events.title: Hamas-led attack on Israel
events.description: Hamas and other militant groups launched a large-scale surprise attack from Gaza into southern Israel, killing about 1,200 people and taking roughly 250 hostages. Israel responded with a major military campaign in Gaza.
events.significance: The attack was the deadliest day for Jews since the Holocaust and triggered a prolonged war with major humanitarian and geopolitical consequences across the Middle East.
